title: Craft First Product Candidate Prototype Chain
objective: Iteratively construct one exact testable Craft product candidate from prototype Definitions and agent-facing ontology scaffolds, collect current product-test evidence, and present one product-approval decision without requesting or inferring any operational authority.

preserved: machine-canonical records with generated human projections
Product Feature, Product Capability, Capability Instance, Bounded Context, directory, implementation, and evidence identity separation
exact source selection, recursion stop, recomposition, and rollback requirements
superseded: semantic admission as a prerequisite for prototype construction
one final request set combining product evaluation with admission or activation
runtime activation and consumer rebinding inside the product-construction chain
predecessor_chain.historical_validation_posture: The predecessor PASS remains valid only for its frozen bytes and former planning contract; it is not current evidence for this successor.

planning_basis.use: Source naming, identity-separation, placement, and migration-scope evidence only; its old phase gates do not override the current D65 construction invariant.

prototype_contract_binding.posture: tested navigation and construction prototype; non-authoritative

construction_invariant.prototype_rule: All stages before product approval are iterative, non-authoritative product-construction work. Changed candidate-bound bytes require a new freeze and current product-test epoch.
construction_invariant.scaffold_rule: Ontology artifacts help agents navigate prototype relations; they do not admit meaning, grant authority, or block unrelated prototype work.
construction_invariant.approval_rule: Product approval is eligible only for one exact frozen product candidate with current passing product-test evidence and has product-approval-only effect.
construction_invariant.post_approval_rule: Authority, admission, activation, cutover, publication, release, deployment, credentials, destructive deletion, and external effects require later separately selected routes and exact owner decisions.

prototype_root.purpose: Keep iterative non-authoritative artifacts together until one exact product candidate is frozen; placement does not create Product Capability, Capability Instance, or Bounded Context identity.
prototype_root.source_direction: Each artifact has one machine-canonical file and a generated human projection. Generated files never become a second authority.
prototype_root.final_placement_posture: Prototype paths do not pre-decide final context or capability-instance placement. Final placement becomes part of the frozen product candidate manifest.

layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether a minimal Craft product vertical can connect explicit prototype meaning to one observable implementation result.
layers.minimum_working_unit: Prototype Definitions, one non-authoritative navigation scaffold, and the smallest Product Capability-to-implementation slice that produces one smoke-test result.
layers.included_scope: Only one provisional capability, minimal business closure, minimal DomainSpec source, one deterministic compiled model, one implementation path, and one smoke witness.
layers.deferred_scope: Completeness, reliability hardening, candidate freeze, full product testing, product approval, and every operational effect.
layers.visible_outcome: An agent and reviewer can trace one intended product behavior from prototype meaning to observable output.
layers.risk_reduced: The architecture may be coherent on paper but incapable of producing a product result.
layers.main_cost_drivers: Prototype schemas, generator, compiler slice, minimal implementation, and smoke-test harness.
layers.exit_evidence: Exact trace closure plus one reproducible smoke result and scaffold non-authority tests.
layers.promotion_decision: Continue to L1 when the thin vertical works; pivot when identities or compilation boundaries fail; stop when no useful product result can be produced.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: Prototype posture, identity separation, source direction, and zero authority effect remain explicit.

layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether the full prototype spine is repeatable, deterministic, failure-aware, and ready to freeze.
layers.minimum_working_unit: All candidate-bound prototype stages reach TESTED_PROTOTYPE under current positive and hostile tests.
layers.included_scope: Iteration across definitions, scaffolds, product, business, DomainSpec, compiled system, implementation, profiles, residue, and rollback.
layers.deferred_scope: Immutable candidate freeze, complete product-test execution, product approval, and operations.
layers.visible_outcome: The same inputs repeatedly produce the same bounded product behavior and evidence.
layers.risk_reduced: A one-off smoke result hides drift, failure, or non-reproducible construction.
layers.main_cost_drivers: Hostile tests, clean-run reproducibility, profile locks, rollback rehearsal, and iteration across the prototype spine.
layers.exit_evidence: All required prototype stages report TESTED_PROTOTYPE with current receipts and typed residue.
layers.promotion_decision: Freeze only when every candidate-bound prototype test passes and residue is explicit.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: The L0 observable behavior and trace closure continue to pass.

layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether one immutable manifest completely identifies the product bytes and tests that will be judged.
layers.minimum_working_unit: One deterministic manifest containing every candidate component, generated output, environment profile, source selector, test contract, and rollback boundary.
layers.included_scope: Exact candidate closure and invalidation rules only.
layers.deferred_scope: Test outcome, approval, activation, migration, and publication.
layers.visible_outcome: Everyone can identify exactly which product is under test.
layers.risk_reduced: Tests or approval drift across changing or partially specified bytes.
layers.main_cost_drivers: Digest closure, final candidate placement, deterministic freeze, and stale-byte detection.
layers.exit_evidence: Frozen manifest reproduces and rejects any changed component.
layers.promotion_decision: Run product tests only against the exact frozen manifest.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: All L0 and L1 tests remain attributable to exact frozen components.

layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether the exact frozen candidate currently passes every required product test and is eligible for product approval.
layers.minimum_working_unit: One collect-all current evidence package covering every required product-test ID for the frozen candidate.
layers.included_scope: Positive, hostile, determinism, stale-byte, rollback, and preapproval-authority-rejection tests.
layers.deferred_scope: Product approval until every required test passes and all operational effects regardless of outcome.
layers.visible_outcome: The Product owner receives a complete current test result for one immutable product.
layers.risk_reduced: Partial validation, stale evidence, or omitted failures are presented as product readiness.
layers.main_cost_drivers: Independent test execution, clean environments, collect-all reporting, and evidence binding.
layers.exit_evidence: All required current outcomes are explicit; approval eligibility is true only when all are PASS.
layers.promotion_decision: Request product approval only for a fully passing current evidence package; otherwise iterate or stop.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: The frozen candidate does not change during testing.

layers.decision_question: After this layer, we know whether the exact tested candidate is approved as the product result, with no operational authority inferred.
layers.minimum_working_unit: One owner decision binding the exact frozen manifest and current complete product-test evidence.
layers.included_scope: Approve, reject, defer, or stop with product-approval-only effect.
layers.deferred_scope: Every authority, admission, activation, cutover, migration, publication, release, deployment, credential, destructive, and external effect.
layers.visible_outcome: A clear Product-owner judgment on the exact tested candidate.
layers.risk_reduced: Passing tests are silently treated as product approval or product approval is inflated into operational permission.
layers.main_cost_drivers: Owner review, exact-byte binding, invalidation rules, and decision evidence.
layers.exit_evidence: A valid decision receipt with product-approval-only effect and empty authority-request references.
layers.promotion_decision: End product construction. Route any desired operational effect separately after approval.
layers.non_regression_guarantee: The approved target and evidence remain immutable; changed bytes require a new candidate, tests, and approval epoch.
layers.next_layer: none inside this chain; operational routes are separate

runnable_now.scope: Author and test the prototype vocabulary, schemas, generated views, and non-collapse fixtures needed by the first thin vertical.

future_frontier_prerequisites.detail: Choose a provisional Product Capability identity and an explicit relation or no-relation posture to the System Construction Product Feature; this does not block prototype Definition work.
Select a prototype Bounded Context placement or an explicit no-context prototype placement rule; directory placement cannot decide.
Select exact dependency-closed CyberAlchemy-v2 and legacy DomainSpec source selectors before importing prototype content.

operational_support.detail: Keep the predecessor chain immutable as historical candidate evidence.
Commit or push the planning package only under a separately authorized publication envelope; untracked planning bytes do not block prototype authoring.
Install nothing until the thin prototype selects an exact language and tool profile. If already available, this task remains non-blocking.

operational_support.owner_route: separately selected governance, implementation, migration, publish, or deployment route
operational_support.detail: Authority, admission, activation, cutover, migration execution, publication, release, deployment, and external effects are not members of this chain.

work_plan.continuation_policy: Continue dependency-ready product construction while unrelated or future operational support remains visible residue.
work_plan.blocking_policy: Only an exact current-frontier prerequisite or applicable safety, privacy, authority, destructive-action, credential, or external-effect boundary may block construction.
work_plan.residue_policy: Record operational support separately and never promote it into product evidence.

required_targets: exact current complete product-test evidence digest
prohibited_members: credentials, destructive actions, or external effects
product_approval_checkpoint.invalidation_rule: Any changed candidate-bound or test-bound byte requires a new candidate freeze, current product-test evidence, and product-approval epoch.

non_regression_guarantees: Machine records remain canonical and every human view is generated.
The predecessor chain remains byte-preserved historical evidence.
Prototype Definitions and ontology scaffolds carry authority_effect none.
Ontology scaffolds help agents navigate but cannot admit, authorize, gate unrelated work, or replace exact source dependencies.
Product Feature, Product Capability, Capability Instance, Bounded Context, directory, implementation, evidence, and approval remain separate identities.
Prototype construction may iterate freely, but an exact product candidate becomes testable only after deterministic freeze.
Product-test PASS does not imply product approval.
Product approval has product-approval-only effect and grants no operational authority.
Operational support never hides a runnable product-construction frontier.
Publication, release, deployment, destructive deletion, credentials, and external effects remain outside this chain.

recommended_next_unit.scope: Author the minimum prototype vocabulary, prototype artifact schema, generated views, and hostile non-collapse fixtures required to build the thin first Craft vertical.
recommended_next_unit.effect_ceiling: prototype product-construction evidence only; no admission, authority, activation, publication, or deployment

claim_ceiling: This successor candidate defines a current prototype-to-tested-product construction chain, two-lane work plan, one product-approval checkpoint, and post-approval operational boundary only. It does not author the prototype artifacts, freeze or test a product candidate, approve a product, create authority, admit meaning or ontology, activate a runtime, migrate or cut over consumers, commit, push, publish, release, deploy, or create an external effect.
